description: Two-layer verification (deterministic gates + reviewer binary rubric) with machine-checkable acceptance-criteria oracles, modeled on Jaymin West's agentic-engineering practice.

userStories.title: Planner produces machine-checkable acceptanceCriteria with oracles
userStories.description: As the cam planner, I need to pair every acceptanceCriterion with an explicit verification method (oracle) so that the implementer and reviewer can mechanically check whether the spec was actually satisfied, defending against the #1 failure mode (spec drift).
acceptanceCriteria: The planner prompt at .claude/agents/subagent-planner.md states that each acceptanceCriterion MUST pair a claim with a verification method (oracle), choosing one of: (a) a named command (e.g. 'bun run typecheck' or 'bun test'), (b) a file-assert (e.g. grep for a string in a file, file existence, JSON-path value), or (c) an explicit 'reviewer-judgment' tag for the irreducibly subjective cases.
The planner prompt documents the litmus quote: 'if you can't test whether the spec was followed, it's too vague' and names spec drift as the #1 failure mode.
The cam-plan command at .claude/commands/cam-plan.md echoes the oracle rule for the user-visible PRD output contract.
The same edits are mirrored to templates/agents/subagent-planner.md and templates/commands/cam-plan.md.
bun run embed-vendor was executed so the embedded copy in src/vendor/_generated.ts is in sync with the templates/ tree.

test/embedded.test.ts (or a sibling test under test/vendor/) asserts that the embedded planner prompt contains the literal oracle litmus quote AND each of the three oracle kinds (named-command, file-assert, reviewer-judgment) is named in the embedded copy. [oracle: bun test on the new assertions]

The story acknowledges that editing .claude/agents/* and templates/* is INTENTIONAL self-hosting of the new contract (not incidental harness drift) so the auditor does not flag it. [oracle: reviewer-judgment]
Vendor drift check passes (bun run embed-vendor:check).
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck).
Tests pass (bun test).
userStories.notes: Files: .claude/agents/subagent-planner.md, .claude/commands/cam-plan.md, templates/agents/subagent-planner.md, templates/commands/cam-plan.md, src/vendor/_generated.ts (regenerated by `bun run embed-vendor`, never hand-edited), test/embedded.test.ts (extend) or new test/vendor/oracle-contract.test.ts. Sources: github.com/jayminwest/overstory (acceptance schema in seeds) + agentic-engineering-book 8-practices/2-evaluation.md + orchestrator memory `agent-eval-research-jaymin-reporter`. Gotchas: (a) templates/ is the source of truth; .claude/ is the runtime mirror — both must be edited; (b) src/vendor/_generated.ts is gated by test/embedded.test.ts (CAM-43 pattern) — never hand-edit, always regenerate; (c) no em-dash in persisted .md (project rule, 2026-05-20).

userStories.title: Auditor enforces the oracle requirement (upgraded C9)
userStories.description: As the cam auditor, I need to BLOCK on any acceptanceCriterion that lacks an oracle so that PRDs which would silently allow spec drift never advance to the implementer.
acceptanceCriteria: The auditor prompt at .claude/agents/subagent-auditor.md upgrades the existing C9 checklist item from 'verifiable' to 'has an oracle': a criterion that pairs no verification method (named command, file-assert, or explicit reviewer-judgment tag) is a finding that the auditor BLOCKs on, not a soft note.
The auditor prompt explicitly names the three accepted oracle kinds (matching US-001's contract): named command, file-assert, reviewer-judgment tag.

The auditor prompt notes that intentional edits to .claude/agents/* and templates/* that are scoped to the active issue (declared in the story body) must NOT be flagged as harness drift; only incidental, undeclared edits are flagged.
The same edits are mirrored to templates/agents/subagent-auditor.md.
bun run embed-vendor was executed so the embedded copy is in sync.

test/embedded.test.ts (or a sibling) asserts the embedded auditor prompt contains the literal phrase 'has an oracle' (or equivalent) AND the BLOCK verb for that finding kind. [oracle: bun test on the new assertion]
Vendor drift check passes (bun run embed-vendor:check).
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck).
Tests pass (bun test).
userStories.notes: Files: .claude/agents/subagent-auditor.md, templates/agents/subagent-auditor.md, src/vendor/_generated.ts (via `bun run embed-vendor`), test/embedded.test.ts (extend). userStories.title: Implementer formalized as Layer A: gate discipline (named command + exitCode 0, roll-up)
userStories.description: As the cam implementer, I need a documented rule that I am PROHIBITED from declaring a story done before its gates pass, and I need to report a roll-up (success/partial/failure by count of passing gates) so that the reviewer (Layer B) can trust the gate signal before judging.
acceptanceCriteria: The implementer prompt at .claude/agents/subagent-implementer.md states explicitly: the implementer is PROHIBITED from declaring a story done before its gates pass.
The implementer prompt defines a gate as: a named command + exitCode 0 (the gate is the COMMAND, not a description).
The implementer prompt defines the roll-up convention: success = all gates pass, partial = some pass / some fail, failure = none pass (or any required gate fails).
The implementer prompt names the two universal mandatory gates already in worker-report.ts ('bun run typecheck', 'bun test') and notes the documented shape lives in src/supervisor/worker-report.ts.

If the documented WorkerReport.gates shape is extended to carry named-command + exitCode + roll-up, src/supervisor/worker-report.ts is updated and a matching test under test/supervisor/ asserts the new shape; if the shape change is NOT strictly needed to express the roll-up, the existing {typecheck, tests} fields are kept and the story documents that decision in the commit message. [oracle: reviewer-judgment on whether the shape change is necessary; bun test on whatever shape is written]
The same prompt edits are mirrored to templates/agents/subagent-implementer.md.
bun run embed-vendor was executed so the embedded copy is in sync.

test/embedded.test.ts (or a sibling) asserts the embedded implementer prompt contains the literal PROHIBITED phrase AND the named-command + exitCode 0 gate definition AND the success/partial/failure roll-up labels. [oracle: bun test on the new assertions]
Vendor drift check passes (bun run embed-vendor:check).
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck).
Tests pass (bun test).

userStories.title: Reviewer as Layer B: binary PASS/FAIL on a fixed 8-criterion rubric with per-criterion evidence
userStories.description: As the cam reviewer, I need to deliver a BINARY PASS/FAIL verdict (not a score) on a FIXED ENUMERATED rubric, walking criterion-by-criterion with cited evidence and explicitly NOT trusting a green test suite, so that the verdict body the orchestrator receives is a structured, auditable judgment (Layer B) and not a vibe-check.
acceptanceCriteria: The reviewer prompt at .claude/agents/subagent-reviewer.md enumerates the 8 fixed rubric criteria, labeled as binary PASS/FAIL: spec-correctness, tests-with-meaningful-assert, strict-types (no unsafe `any`), error-handling, project-conventions, security, deps, perf.
The reviewer prompt requires the reviewer to walk the rubric criterion-by-criterion and cite EVIDENCE (file path + line range, or a quoted snippet) per criterion.
The reviewer prompt states explicitly that a green test suite does NOT imply PASS on spec-correctness or tests-with-meaningful-assert (passing != correct; the agent may have gamed the test).

The reviewer prompt defines the hard-constraint rule: any hard constraint failure (won't compile, missing required field, security violation) FAILs the whole verdict regardless of soft-rubric count; the soft rubric is the count of satisfied criteria for triage but does NOT promote a hard FAIL to PASS.

The reviewer prompt and cam-review command at .claude/commands/cam-review.md document the verdict BODY shape: { status: 'PASS' | 'FAIL', justification: <prose>, itemizedFailures: [<by-criterion>] } and state that this body is the payload the CAM-55 report-on-exit pushes to the orchestrator.

The reviewer prompt explicitly preserves the existing terminal signal: the <review>CLEAN</review> / <review>FIXES_PENDING:N</review> tag and parseReviewVerdict (src/supervisor/result.ts:197) remain exactly as-is. The new structured body is the PAYLOAD of the report, not a replacement of the sentinel.
The same edits are mirrored to templates/agents/subagent-reviewer.md and templates/commands/cam-review.md.
bun run embed-vendor was executed so the embedded copy is in sync.

test/embedded.test.ts (or a sibling) asserts the embedded reviewer prompt contains all 8 rubric criterion names verbatim, the 'evidence per criterion' instruction, the 'does not trust green tests' clause, and the hard-constraint-fail-the-whole rule. [oracle: bun test on the new assertions]
A reviewer reads the rubric as a criterion-by-criterion walk (not a free-form checklist) and the verdict body shape is unambiguous. [oracle: reviewer-judgment]
Vendor drift check passes (bun run embed-vendor:check).
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck).
Tests pass (bun test).
